title: Federal money through the City, organization by organization
question: Which organizations’ audits show the most federal money from the City that the City’s own subaward reports do not show?
finding: Of 86 organizations whose audits show $250,000 or more received through the City, 21 with $1 million or more ($158.1 million together) are named in no City subaward report. The largest differences: Children's Council of San Francisco ($77.3 million audited, $275,000 reported); Episcopal Community Svcs of SF Inc ($66.4 million audited, $2.2 million reported); Healthright 360 ($56.4 million audited, $319,002 reported); The Yerba Buena Gardens Conservancy ($52.9 million audited, $0 reported); Heluna Health ($45.4 million audited, $288,133 reported).
how: Recipients’ audits (award lines naming the City as pass-through body, fiscal years ending 2019 to 2025) against the City’s subaward reports dated July 2018 to December 2025, summed by organization. A City subaward report is tied to an organization by the federal entity number the clearinghouse gives for its employer number (640 report rows), otherwise by normalised name (256 rows); 198 rows name recipients outside the set and are left out of this table. The last column lists programmes with $50,000 or more in the audits and nothing in the reports.
limits: The readings set out under the programme screen apply here too, plus one of matching: a subaward reported under a partnership or affiliate name that does not carry the organization’s entity number is not counted, which makes the reported figure too low for housing developers. A name match is used only where the City is the payer on both sides. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.
